selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: In the first short poem, what image is used for the universe?
questions.answer: It is pictured like a written book full of meaning.

questions.question: Why does the passage speak about the world as if it were a book?
questions.answer: To show that the world can be read for signs, lessons, and proofs.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the clarity of those signs to the heart?
questions.answer: It describes them as shining clearly before the heart’s understanding.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the statement that no dark point remains?
questions.answer: The signs of Allah are made very clear for anyone sincere in reflection.

questions.question: According to the passage, are the signs in creation few or many? Explain.
questions.answer: They are many beyond counting, because the passage speaks of endless pages and countless works.

questions.question: What can a reader infer about the order of the world from the idea of a preserved record?
questions.answer: The world follows a known and purposeful order.

questions.question: What central message do all things announce together?
questions.answer: They declare that only Allah deserves worship.

questions.question: Which quality of Allah is emphasized by the words calling on the Living One?
questions.answer: His everlasting life.

questions.question: How does the final response of the heart and nafs strengthen the passage’s message?
questions.answer: It shows that both reflection and inner recognition lead to accepting the truth.

questions.question: What is the best summary of the final line of the marked passage?
questions.answer: The person’s heart and self both accept the truth shown by creation.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the whole marked passage?
questions.answer: All of creation points clearly to the oneness of Allah.

questions.question: What is the role of the “pen” in the passage’s picture?
questions.answer: It represents divine power bringing signs and forms into existence.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the “heart’s eye” instead of only the physical eye?
questions.answer: Because recognizing these truths needs inner understanding, not just looking.

questions.question: What effect does this image have on the reader’s view of nature and the world?
questions.answer: It encourages the reader to see the world as full of evidence of Allah.

questions.question: What relationship does the passage show between beings and meaning?
questions.answer: It shows that every being carries meaning like a word in a message.

questions.question: How is every created thing described in relation to meaning?
questions.answer: Each thing is presented like a meaningful word that shows a message.

questions.question: When all things speak together, what belief are they united on?
questions.answer: They are united on the truth that Allah is One.

questions.question: What key belief is directly stated near the end of the passage?
questions.answer: That Allah is One.

questions.question: How do the heart and nafs model the right response to these signs?
questions.answer: They listen, understand, and agree with the truth.

questions.question: What object from everyday reading is used to help explain the universe?
questions.answer: A book or written page.

questions.question: Who is shown as the One behind those signs?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: In the poem, what writes the signs seen in the universe?
questions.answer: Divine power is described as writing them.

questions.question: What do the endless leaves and many lines suggest about the universe?
questions.answer: They suggest that the universe contains unending signs and lessons.

questions.question: What are the “lines” in that book said to be?
questions.answer: They are the many events that happen through time.
